children: Chinese e-commerce titan JD.com reported mixed third-quarter results as it sought to expand its food-delivery footprint and make headway in overseas markets.

The Beijing-based company is in recovery mode after a brutal price war in the domestic food-delivery market. China's weak macroeconomic picture has only piled pressure on its core retail business, which is also contending with a high base last year, when government subsidies boosted sales.

The online retailer on Tuesday said net profit reached 6.50 billion yuan, equivalent to $975.2 million, for the three months ended September. That was 23% higher than a year earlier but fell 8.8% from the previous quarter.
Revenue rose 3.5% from a year ago to 309.59 billion yuan.
Analysts had expected net profit of 7.265 billion yuan on revenue of 308.12 billion yuan, according to a FactSet consensus estimate.

Ahead of the results, Jefferies analysts estimated food-delivery losses to have more than halved in the third quarter from a year earlier, while Citi cautioned that intense competition in China's e-commerce and food-delivery markets remained a risk to the company's share price.
